stations.name: Bottleneck Buster
stations.goal: Measure a real application and make it at least 5x faster.
stations.why: Measuring instead of guessing is how performance engineers work. It is the foundation for everything after.
checks: Is there a profile (flamegraph, perf, Nsight, etc.) before and after the change?
Is the speedup at least 5x with identical results?
Is there a test proving identical outputs?
stations.proof: PR or README with a before/after measurement and the command to reproduce it.
steps: Pick a program you know that is noticeably slow.
Take a profile and find the hottest section.
Change, re-measure, repeat until 5x is reached.
Put the measurements into the README as a table.

stations.name: Backward Thinker
stations.goal: Build automatic differentiation yourself and train a small network with it.
stations.why: Autodiff is the engine of every AI library. Whoever built one really understands training.
checks: Is there a compute-graph structure with a backward pass?
Do the gradients match numerical differences (gradient check)?
Does a small network (for example digits) learn with it?
stations.proof: Repo with a gradient-check test and a training curve.
steps: Build scalar operations with backward rules.
Write the gradient check as a test.
Train a network on a small dataset.

stations.name: Spark From Nothing
stations.goal: Train a transformer from scratch with your own training loop.
stations.why: Shows that you can build modern models, not only apply them.
checks: Are there your own attention, block and training implementations (no ready-made model)?
Does the loss fall in a traceable way?
Is there an evaluation on test data?
stations.proof: Repo with configuration, curve and sample outputs.
steps: Build the model block by block.
Training loop with optimizer and schedule.

stations.name: Master Teacher
stations.goal: Explain a hard topic so that others understand it: an article or video with 10,000 views.
stations.why: Being able to explain is the rarest skill in a team. Reach proves it lands.
checks: Is there a public piece with technical content?
Does the platform show at least 10,000 views?
stations.proof: Link to the piece (the number is confirmed by you).
steps: Pick a topic you just learned.

stations.name: Silicon Smith
stations.goal: Write your own GPU kernel that keeps up with the library version in a benchmark.
stations.why: Hardware-near performance is the core business of every GPU company.
checks: Is there a kernel in CUDA, Triton or similar?
Is there a reproducible comparison with a library function?
Is your kernel at 80% or more of the reference?
stations.proof: Repo with benchmark script and results table.
steps: Optimize step by step (tiling, shared memory).
Document every step with a number.

stations.name: Roofline Rider
stations.goal: Show whether a kernel is limited by compute or memory bandwidth, and rebuild it accordingly.
stations.why: Whoever knows the limits of the hardware optimizes deliberately instead of randomly.
checks: Is there a roofline analysis with measurement points?
Did a change measurably move the point closer to the limit?
stations.proof: Diagram and measurement data in the repo.
steps: Determine compute and bandwidth of the card.
Plot the kernel in the diagram.

stations.name: Light Bender
stations.goal: Build a ray tracer that renders a scene interactively.
stations.why: Graphics combines maths, parallelism and performance, exactly what graphics teams look for.
checks: Are there ray-object intersection, light and shadows?
Does a scene run at 10 frames per second or more?
Is there an acceleration structure (BVH or similar)?
steps: Move it to the GPU or multiple cores.

stations.name: Bit Alchemist
stations.goal: Bring a model to INT8 or INT4 and lose less than 1% accuracy.
stations.why: Efficient inference saves cost and power in practice.
checks: Is there quantization code or a documented pipeline?
Is the accuracy loss below 1%?
Is the model measurably faster or smaller?
stations.proof: Table with accuracy, size and speed.
steps: Fix the base model and the measurement.
Calibrate and win back the lost accuracy.

stations.name: Second Voice
stations.goal: Rebuild a published paper and document deviations honestly.
stations.why: Reproducing shows scientific care, not just programming.
checks: Is there a reimplementation referencing the paper?
Are results and deviations compared in a table?
stations.proof: Repo with comparison table and discussion.
steps: Pick a paper with a clear result.
Rebuild the method step by step.

stations.name: Shadow Translator
stations.goal: Build a small shader compiler that translates a high-level language into an intermediate format.
stations.why: Compiler knowledge is rare and central to graphics and AI drivers.
checks: Are there a parser, intermediate representation and code generation?
Does an example shader run with it?
steps: Generate target code and run it.

stations.name: Sandstorm
stations.goal: A particle or fluid simulation with over 1 million elements in real time on the GPU.
stations.why: Massively parallel simulation is a prime example of GPU work.
checks: Does the simulation run on the GPU?
Are there at least 1M elements at 30 frames per second or more?
steps: Simple particle system on the GPU.

stations.name: The Marathon Runner
stations.goal: Build an inference server with batching, caching and streaming that stays stable under load.
stations.why: Operating under load separates prototypes from products.
checks: Is there dynamic batching and caching?
Is there a load test with throughput and latency?
Does it stay stable for 1 hour?
steps: Serve the model as a service.

stations.name: Judge of Models
stations.goal: Publish a reproducible benchmark that others use.
stations.why: Good measurement shapes what counts as good.
checks: Are there a dataset, metrics and scripts?
Have at least 3 foreign repos or papers used it?

stations.name: Flaw in the Foundation
stations.goal: Find and fix a bug in a large compiler, runtime or library.
stations.why: Finding bugs in foundations takes deep understanding and patience.
checks: Is there an issue with a minimal example from you?
Is your fix merged?
steps: Pick a project you already use.
Reduce odd behaviour to the smallest case.
Find the cause in the code.
Submit the fix with a test.

stations.name: Touched the Heart
stations.goal: Get a PR merged into the core of a world-class project (for example a large AI or compiler library).
stations.why: The most public seal of quality: strangers who maintain it trust your code.
checks: Is the PR merged in a project with more than 20,000 stars?
Does it touch core code (not only docs)?

stations.name: Swarm Computer
stations.goal: Distribute training or inference across multiple GPUs with near-linear scaling.
stations.why: Scaling is the everyday problem of large models.
checks: Does it run on 2 or more GPUs?
Is the scaling efficiency 80% or more?

stations.name: Better Idea
stations.goal: Develop your own variant (optimizer, attention, compression) that is measurably better on a recognized benchmark.
stations.why: Proving your own ideas is the step from application to research.
checks: Is there an ablation study?
Is the improvement statistically clear over several runs?
stations.proof: Repo with scripts and results over 3 or more runs.
steps: Find a weakness in a known method.

stations.name: Nanosecond Nomad
stations.goal: Build a service with p99 latency under 10 ms at over 10,000 requests per second.
stations.why: Low latency under load needs deep systems knowledge.
checks: Is there a reproducible load test?
Is p99 below 10 ms at 10,000 RPS or more?

stations.name: Iron Heart
stations.goal: Get your own kernel or device driver running on real hardware.
stations.why: The direct line to the hardware is rare and in high demand.
checks: Is there boot code or a driver?
Is there evidence that it runs on real hardware?
steps: Start with a microcontroller or an emulator.

stations.name: The Parliament
stations.goal: Build a distributed system with consensus that survives chaos tests.
stations.why: Distributed correctness is one of the hardest topics in computer science.
checks: Are there leader election and log replication?
Does the data stay consistent through node failures?

stations.name: Gap Reader
stations.goal: Find a security vulnerability and report it with a CVE number.
stations.why: Responsible handling of vulnerabilities is highly regarded.
checks: Is there a CVE with your name?
steps: Pick a project with a bug bounty or security policy.

stations.name: The Stage
stations.goal: Give a technical talk at a conference or meetup.
stations.why: Shows that you can pass knowledge on.
checks: Is there a public programme with your name?
stations.proof: Link to the programme or video.
steps: Pick a topic from one of your own projects.

stations.name: Gatekeeper
stations.goal: Get write access (maintainer) in a project with over 10,000 stars.
stations.why: The highest trust a community can give.
checks: Are you listed as maintainer or committer?
Does the project have more than 10,000 stars?
stations.proof: Entry in the maintainers file or org membership.
